title: ProgramIR node set v0.4 (SEM-8)
description: The forward grammar's JSON encoding, spec/node-set.md SEM-8 ruling as amended by the ratified v0.2 ergonomics batch (D-034), v0.3 values batch (D-037, 2026-08-10), and v0.4 inputs-bag admission (D-041, 2026-08-11): the `node` discriminator, the statement/expression vocabulary below, leaves as {leaf: {kind, ref?}} with the interpreter leaf carrying a required ref (D-029), dynamic tools as {leaf: {kind: 'tool'}, name: <expr>}. v0.2 added statements SetIndex/AssignTuple, expressions IfExp/BoolOp/UnaryOp/Format/List/Dict/Index, the For list-iter form, and the widened Compare/BinOp operator enums. v0.3 adds statements Pass/Log, the Slice expression, and two pure call forms (builtin table, value-method table); the aforward rule (D-037) makes async twins lower to this identical vocabulary. v0.4 adds the record envelope (args as exactly one record binding, bound to the module's own input signature, D-036 component 2) and the leaf-call `splat` field (the signature-record splat; LM-decided dicts stay refused). Artifact form carries no source spans (SEM-8: refusal locations are an input-side concern). The root of this schema is one forward object -- the input to the node_compile op (harness/PROTOCOL.md). Anything outside this closed vocabulary refuses at compile with PIR-E-NODE-* (spec/errors.md).

identifier.description: A simple name. Assign targets are simple names (spec/node-set.md SEM-5 ruling, amended v0.2: tuple destructuring is the AssignTuple statement, subscript writes are the SetIndex statement; attribute targets refuse at compile).

forward.description: One module's forward, spec/manifest.md component 5: the language tag, the argument names, and the statement body (spec/node-set.md SEM-8 v0 envelope, from examples 13-15).

language.description: The v0 language tag adopted by SEM-8 from the observed corpus. The vocabulary is this contract's own, operationally defined and CPython-independent, despite the historical name.

args.description: The forward's parameter list ('self' excluded), in exactly one of two forms (v0.4, D-041): the plain form -- input names as identifier strings (the SEM-8 v0 envelope) -- or the record envelope -- exactly ONE record binding object, def forward(self, inputs). A record beside plain names is not a lawful envelope (unobserved, so refused; PIR-E-NODE-001).

oneOf.description: Plain form: the declared input names (SEM-8 v0 envelope).
Record envelope (v0.4, D-041): exactly one record binding, the whole parameter list. minItems keeps the empty list unambiguous (it is the plain form).

body.description: The statement list; at least one statement (a forward must produce its Prediction via Return, spec/node-set.md statement whitelist).

record_binding.description: The record envelope's one parameter (v0.4, D-041): the module's own input record, def forward(self, inputs). The record's key set is STATIC -- exactly the input fields of the module signature it binds (D-036 component 2), in declared field order; the forward restates nothing. The record is read-only (any Assign/AssignTuple/For-target/SetIndex naming it refuses PIR-E-NODE-004) and shallowly immutable at execution.

name.description: The record parameter's name -- what Attr reads, and what a leaf call's `splat` may reference.

record.description: The binding target: the module's OWN input signature (D-036 component 2). 'self' is the only lawful target in v0.4 -- an explicit const so any future target is a visible versioned extension, never a reinterpretation of a bare name.

statement.description: A whitelisted statement, spec/node-set.md statement whitelist, discriminated on `node`. Statements: Assign, AssignTuple, SetIndex, Return, If, For, While, Break, Continue, Try, Raise (AssignTuple/SetIndex v0.2, D-034), Pass, Log (v0.3, D-037).

expression.description: A whitelisted expression, discriminated on `node`. Expressions: Call (leaf, builtin, or method form), Attr, Var, Const, Compare, BinOp, IfExp, BoolOp, UnaryOp, Format, List, Dict, Index (v0.2, D-034), Slice (v0.3, D-037). spec/node-set.md SEM-8; SEM-4 pins the operator subsets and call forms.

stmt_assign.description: Assign: thread values between leaf calls (spec/node-set.md whitelist). Target is a single simple name (SEM-5 ruling); no attribute/global mutation.

target.description: The bound name, SEM-5 ruling: simple names only.

stmt_return.description: Return: the module output, a Prediction (spec/node-set.md whitelist; PIR-013: Prediction fields = declared output fields exactly).

value.description: The returned expression. v0 encodes this as an expression node (examples 13-15); the bare-string form of example 01 is pre-v0 and fails here.

stmt_if.description: If: data-dependent branch (spec/node-set.md whitelist). The test must evaluate to a boolean at runtime; any other value raises InterpreterTypeError -- no truthiness table (SEM-1 ruling).

test.description: The condition; boolean at runtime per SEM-1 ruling.

body.description: The then-branch; non-empty (the source form cannot author an empty block and v0 has no pass node).

orelse.description: The else-branch; may be empty (observed form always carries the key).

stmt_for.description: For: bounded loop (spec/node-set.md whitelist), in exactly one of two forms (SEM-2 ruling, amended v0.2): the range form {node, target, range, body} iterating range(<non-negative int literal>), or the list form {node, target, iter, body} whose `iter` expression must evaluate to a list, iterated as a shallow snapshot taken at loop entry (mutation during iteration affects the list, never the iteration; non-list raises InterpreterTypeError). Bounded by its literal or the list length (SEM-6). for/else is not representable.

target.description: The loop variable, a simple name (SEM-2/SEM-5).

range.description: Range form: the literal iteration count, range(<non-negative int literal>) (SEM-2 ruling).

iter.description: List form (v0.2): an expression evaluating to a list; shallow snapshot at loop entry (SEM-2 ruling as amended).

stmt_while.description: While: condition-driven loop (spec/node-set.md whitelist). Boolean test per SEM-1. Interpretation-side default cap of 1000 iterations; breach raises LoopCapError, a harness guard NOT catchable by program handlers (SEM-6 ruling -- v0 carries no per-loop override field). while/else is not representable.

test.description: The condition; boolean at runtime per SEM-1 ruling.

stmt_break.description: Break: exit the innermost loop (spec/node-set.md whitelist).

stmt_continue.description: Continue: next iteration of the innermost loop (spec/node-set.md whitelist; emitted by the ex-15 reference compiler, hence in the v0 observed vocabulary).

stmt_try.description: Try: error + recovery flow over typed errors (spec/node-set.md whitelist; SEM-3 ruling). try/finally and try/else are not representable (v0, per the ex-15 compiler).

handlers.description: The handler list; at least one (a Try without handlers is meaningless in v0 -- no finally/else forms).

except_handler.description: One except clause. Handler matching is exact name, or 'Exception' which catches every table error -- including Raise'd ones, which flow through the same channel as leaf errors (SEM-3 ruling). Binding the caught error to a name is not representable (v0).

type.description: The caught type: the SEM-3 typed-error table plus 'Exception', which catches every table error. The v0.2 error-table amendment (D-034) adds InterpreterTypeError, InterpreterKeyError, and InterpreterArithmeticError as exact-matchable names, resolving the former catchability tension. LoopCapError and MalformedNodeError are deliberately absent -- harness guards, never catchable (SEM-6 ruling).

stmt_raise.description: Raise: throw a typed error (spec/node-set.md whitelist). Raise-able names are restricted to the SEM-3 table -- an unknown name is a compile refusal, never a runtime fallback. Only the `raise SomeError(<constant>)` source form is representable (ex-15 compiler); example 14's `ValueError` is pre-ratification and fails here (see schema/README.md).

exc.description: The raised type: exactly the SEM-3 typed-error table.

message.description: The constant carried by the raise (the ex-15 compiler admits any constant; observed messages are strings). Carried data only -- refusal/trace comparison never matches message text (spec/errors.md discipline).

leaf.description: A Call's declared leaf: {kind, ref?} (SEM-8 ruling). Every Call resolves to a declared, typed leaf -- Predict, sub-module, tool/UDF, or interpreter -- or compile refuses naming the call (spec/node-set.md leaf rule; PIR-E-NODE-002). Kind-specific ref requirements are enforced on the Call node ($defs/expr_call).

kind.description: The leaf type, spec/node-set.md leaf rule.

ref.description: The declared target: a child Predict name (kind=predict), a sub-module name (kind=module), a component-6 tool name (kind=tool, static form), or a component-7 interpreter pool entry name (kind=interpreter; REQUIRED by D-029 -- the examples' ref-less interpreter leaf is pre-ratification; the migrator adds ref: 'main').

expr_call.description: Call: invoke a declared leaf (spec/node-set.md leaf rule). Arguments are keywords only -- positional args and **splat are not representable (ex-15 compiler; example 01's args: '**inputs' is pre-v0 and fails). Dynamic tool dispatch (tools[name](...)) is the model-dispatched call convention: {leaf: {kind: 'tool'}, name: <expr>}, unknown names raising a catchable typed ToolError (SEM-8 ruling).

kwargs.description: Keyword arguments: name -> expression. Always present, possibly empty (the observed v0 form).

name.description: Dynamic tool dispatch ONLY: the expression evaluating to the tool's name at runtime (SEM-8: dynamic tools as {leaf: {kind: 'tool'}, name: <expr>}). Forbidden on every other leaf kind -- enforced by the allOf below.

splat.description: Record-splat (v0.4, D-041): the name of the forward's record parameter, whose signature-defined key set merges into this call's kwargs -- expanded keys first (declared field order), then the explicit kwargs (authored order). Lawful ONLY when it names the forward's declared record (compile checks; a splat of anything else -- an LM-decided dict -- refuses PIR-E-NODE-002 naming the target). A splat/kwarg collision refuses PIR-E-NODE-003 naming the key. One splat per call by construction; absent on the builtin/method call forms (closed objects).

allOf.description: predict/module/interpreter leaves: ref required (D-029 for interpreter), dynamic `name` forbidden.
tool leaves: exactly one of static ref (leaf.ref, no `name`) or dynamic dispatch (`name`, no leaf.ref).

oneOf.description: Static tool call: leaf names a component-6 entry.
Dynamic (model-dispatched) tool call: name expression, no ref.

expr_attr.description: Attr: field access on a Prediction/record held in a variable -- only simple `var.field` access is representable (ex-15 compiler; SEM-7 ruling: key lookup, a missing key raises typed catchable InterpreterKeyError, never a raw host exception).

obj.description: The variable name holding the record. NOTE: a bare name string, not an expression node -- the v0 observed encoding.

expr_var.description: Var: read a bound name. An unbound Var raises InterpreterKeyError (SEM-7 ruling).

expr_const.description: Const: a literal. Values flowing between leaves are JSON values, Prediction records, and typed errors (SEM-7 ruling); Const literals are the JSON scalars -- container literals are the dedicated List/Dict expression nodes (v0.2).

value.description: The literal value, a JSON scalar (SEM-7; int/float distinction follows the serde profile, PIR-004).

expr_compare.description: Compare: single comparison (spec/node-set.md whitelist, closed operator subset; SEM-4 ruling as amended v0.2). eq/ne is JSON-value equality (different JSON types unequal, never an error; objects order-insensitive, lists ordered); lt/le/gt/ge compares number-with-number mathematically exactly and string-with-string by Unicode code point; in/not_in is the v0.2 membership table (needle in list, substring, string in dict = key presence). Other operand pairings raise InterpreterTypeError. Chained comparisons are not representable (frontend desugar only).

op.description: The comparison operator, SEM-4 ruling's closed subset as amended v0.2 (D-034).

right.description: Right operand (exactly one comparator in v0).

expr_binop.description: BinOp: binary operation (SEM-4 ruling as amended v0.2). `add` is string+string concatenation, number+number addition, or list+list concatenation (fresh backing store); sub/mult/div follow the v0.2 arithmetic rules -- int exactness to +/-2^63-1, InterpreterArithmeticError on int overflow, zero divisor, non-finite float results, or div with an int operand beyond 2^53. `mod` is not admitted. Any other operand pairing raises InterpreterTypeError at runtime; other operators refuse at compile.

op.description: The binary operator, SEM-4 ruling's closed set as amended v0.2 (D-034).

stmt_assigntuple.description: AssignTuple (v0.2, D-034): destructuring bind. The value must evaluate to a list of exactly len(targets) elements (InterpreterTypeError otherwise); targets bind left to right. Tuple values do not exist -- frontends lower tuple literals to lists. Single-name binds are Assign; a one-target AssignTuple is unobserved and refuses (refusing is cheaper than specifying).

targets.description: The bound names, left to right; simple names only (SEM-5 ruling as amended).

value.description: The destructured expression; must evaluate to a list of exactly len(targets) elements.

stmt_setindex.description: SetIndex (v0.2, D-034): subscript write, the ReAct trajectory idiom (trajectory[key] = v). Target names a variable holding a dict (insert-or-overwrite, string keys, overwrite keeps the key's original insertion position) or a list (existing index only). In-place mutation per the v0.2 aliasing ruling -- visible through every variable bound to the container. Errors as Index: missing/out-of-range key InterpreterKeyError, other pairings InterpreterTypeError. Prediction records are not dicts here (SEM-7 as amended).

target.description: The variable name holding the mutated container (a bare name string, matching Attr's obj convention).

key.description: The key expression: a string for dict targets, an int for list targets.

expr_ifexp.description: IfExp (encoding pinned v0.2, D-034 -- closes the v0 spec/schema contradiction): conditional expression. Evaluate test (boolean, SEM-1); evaluate and yield exactly one branch; the untaken branch is never evaluated.

test.description: The condition; boolean at runtime per SEM-1 ruling.

body.description: Yielded when the test is true.

orelse.description: Yielded when the test is false.

expr_boolop.description: BoolOp (encoding pinned v0.2, D-034 -- closes the v0 spec/schema contradiction): and/or over two or more boolean operands (SEM-1's rule); short-circuit left to right; unevaluated operands are never type-checked.

values.description: The operands, evaluated left to right with short-circuit.

expr_unaryop.description: UnaryOp (v0.2, D-034): `not` on booleans; `neg` on numbers, with neg 0.0 yielding 0.0 (-0.0 is kept out of the value model); anything else raises InterpreterTypeError.

expr_format.description: Format (v0.2, D-034): string building, the f-string / template-literal / Sprintf compile target. Evaluate parts left to right; string values pass through verbatim; int values render in canonical decimal (optional leading '-', digits, no leading zeros, no '+', no grouping); anything else (float, bool, null, container) raises InterpreterTypeError. Concatenate. Floats are deliberately excluded until a cross-language float repr is pinned (v0.3 candidate).

parts.description: The concatenated parts, evaluated left to right.

expr_list.description: List (v0.2, D-034): list literal. Evaluate items in order; yield a fresh list (a reference value under the aliasing ruling). May be empty -- the comprehension desugar's seed.

items.description: The element expressions, evaluated in order; may be empty.

expr_dict.description: Dict (v0.2, D-034): object literal. Keys are expressions evaluating to strings (InterpreterTypeError otherwise); a later duplicate key overwrites the value but keeps the key's original insertion position; insertion order is preserved and observable in serialized output. Equality: objects compare order-insensitively; lists compare ordered. May be empty (trajectory = {}). Go engines need an ordered-map value type; map[string]any is non-conforming.

key.description: The key expression; must evaluate to a string.

entries.description: The entries in authoring order; may be empty.

stmt_pass.description: Pass (v0.3, D-037): no-op statement; exists so frontends compile empty blocks without inventing filler.

stmt_log.description: Log (v0.3, D-037): print's lawful home. Parts follow Format's argument rules; the rendered string is written to the run's observability trace (_trajectory overlay), NEVER to program state -- fixtures assert Log cannot affect any subsequent value.

parts.description: The logged parts, Format's evaluation and rendering rules.

expr_slice.description: Slice (v0.3, D-037): read-only slice of a list or string. Python clamping semantics (out-of-range clamps, never errors); negative indices count from the end; absent start/stop mean the ends; step admitted only as literal 1 or -1 (any other step is a compile refusal, hence the const forms). Yields a fresh list/string. Slice assignment is NOT admitted.

obj.description: The sliced list or string expression (other runtime types raise InterpreterTypeError).

start.description: Optional start index expression (int at runtime; negative counts from the end).

stop.description: Optional stop index expression (int at runtime; negative counts from the end).

step.description: Literal step, 1 (default when absent) or -1. Non-literal or other steps refuse at compile.

expr_call_builtin.description: Builtin call (v0.3, D-037): {node:'Call', builtin, args} -- the closed pure-builtin table; unknown names refuse at compile (PIR-E-NODE-*). All entries are pure functions of their operands; semantics pinned in spec/node-set.md v0.3 (len/str/int/float/max/min/sum/sorted/any/all, json_dumps/json_parse bound to the canonical-JSON serde profile). str/float rendering follows the float-repr pin.

builtin.description: The builtin name, the closed v0.3 table.

args.description: Positional argument expressions, evaluated left to right.

expr_call_method.description: Value-method call (v0.3, D-037): {node:'Call', method, obj, args} -- the closed str/list/dict method table; unknown names refuse at compile. Receiver type checked at runtime (InterpreterTypeError on mismatch); list/dict mutators follow the v0.2 aliasing ruling; str methods yield fresh values with code-point semantics; case mapping is Unicode simple-case, locale-free. Semantics pinned in spec/node-set.md v0.3.

method.description: The method name, the closed v0.3 table (str/list/dict families; receiver type resolves the family at runtime).

args.description: Positional argument expressions; may be empty (e.g. no-arg strip/pop/keys).

expr_index.description: Index (v0.2, D-034): subscript read. Dict + string key -> member, missing -> InterpreterKeyError. List + int key -> 0-based element; negative or out-of-range -> InterpreterKeyError. Any other obj/key pairing -> InterpreterTypeError. Prediction records are not dicts here -- only Attr reads them (SEM-7 as amended).

key.description: The key expression: a string for dicts, an int for lists.
